newsitem.title: USA: Leslie-ADM pegs US corn 8.906 bln bu, soy 2.30 bln.
newsitem.headline: Leslie-ADM pegs US corn 8.906 bln bu, soy 2.30 bln.

text.p: The Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator survey Monday estimated U.S. corn production based on Oct 1 conditions at 8,906,484,000 bushels and soybeans at 2,302,329,000 bushels, versus 8,889,508,000 bu of corn and 2,244,760,000 bu of soybeans Leslie estimated last month.
The estimates are based on inquiries with 1,200 grain elevators in the Corn Belt.

The estimates compare with U.S. Agriculture Department's Sept 1 estimates of 8,803,928,000 bu corn and 2,269,505,000 bu soybeans. U.S. corn production in 1995 totaled 7,373,876,000 bu and soybeans 2,151,834,000 bu.
U.S. average production for the past five years has been 8,152,954,000 bu corn and 2,143,000,000 bu soybeans.
Leslie pegged average corn yield at 121.6 bushels per acre against last month's estimate of 121.3 bushels an acre, the five-year average of 118.6 and last year's 113.5 bushels.
Leslie said the corn crop remains late, with only 56 percent of the plants mature at Oct 1 against the normal 82 percent.
Leslie pegged end-season carryout on Aug 31, 1997, at 777 million bushels, against 709 million seen last month and 426 million a year earlier, based on current demand estimates by USDA.
Leslie pegged average soybean yield at 36.3 bushels an acre against last month's estimate of 35.4 bushels, the five-year average of 36.1 and last year's 34.9 bushels.

Based on USDA demand and stocks estimates, Leslie pegged end-stocks of soybeans on Aug 31, 1997, at 200 million bushels compared to 115 million seen last month and 183 million on August 31, 1996, based on current demand estimates by USDA.

Leslie said only 56 percent of U.S. soybeans had dropped leaves by Oct 1 against 71 pct normally. Harvest was also well behind in all major Midwest states except Iowa, which was 17 percent harvested against 15 pct on a 5-year average.
"Important areas received early frosts during the first week of October," Leslie said. "No adjustments have been made for those developments."
